## II. INDEX OF MEMORABLE SUBJECTS AND EXPOSITIONS

[Col. 1653]

### A

Perfect self-denial and renunciation of the world is a greater work than the creation of the world, 314. The hidden things of this life are first revealed in the next, 609. The abyss can signify angels, 551. How Christ, the growing Son of the Lord, is understood, 751, 755. From the slothful, even what they have will be taken away, 214. And blessing is removed from them, 339. A silver bowl signifies a body attenuated by works of repentance, 635. Wicked Ahaz thinks despairingly concerning God’s mercy, 193. In what perfection and for what end Adam was created by God, 724. He is a prophet, 664. He owes more to God than Eve does, 443. He is compared to a fountain, 551. And he is disobedient to another’s vice, 290. The young man can be understood as a figure of Christ’s humanity, 649, 653. In what does true worship consist? 71. It consists in humility, 451. Every sinner may be called an adulterer before God, 523. By God’s grace we bear adversity and prosperity meritoriously and with equanimity, 219, 270. And we lead them to the right hand, 270. They make us worthy of heaven, 453. The four ages of human beings figure Daniel’s four prophetic beasts, 713. Consideration of eternal things produces and preserves patience in us, 743. Saint Agatha is rich through possession of the precious pearl, 133. The lamb signifies repentance, 391; likewise simplicity, meekness, and patience, 392. The six wings of the seraphim denote faith, hope, and charity; likewise thoughts, words, and works, 699. The altar denotes angels, 664; likewise the human body and soul, 668; and purity of the senses, 727. How one loving one’s soul loses it, and conversely preserves it, 464. Christ’s walking beside the sea is his joyful working of human redemption, 1 and 2. It also means proceeding with a gentle step, 2 and 578. Supernatural love is God’s greatest gift, 47. Without it no virtue endures, 77. It succeeds fear, 12, 85. It must be joined to fear, 183, and never lost, 237. It obtains pardon and mercy, 151; and filial love toward God inherits heaven, 78. Fear is owed to the Creator, love to the Redeemer, 149. The latter is set forth in the word “Son,” the former in the voice “Child,” 36, 43. Both are a sword sharpened on either side, 236. Worldly love separates the human heart from God, 630. See “Charity” or “Love.” God shows his love to sinners, 216. Angels are God’s altars, 664; governors of virtues, 707; our neighbors, kinsmen, and protectors, 383; our brothers, 737; and sisters, 20, 22. They bear Jesus for us, 117. They stand by those celebrating his Nativity, 20. Very many accompany Gabriel to the Virgin Mary, 201, 547. They are in some way saddened that their number in heaven is not complete, 185. Hence they fight for us in temptations, 207. They assist the dying, 548. They lead the souls of the righteous into heaven, 117, and rejoice at their exaltation, 383, no less than at repentance, 737. But they strip the impenitent of heavenly gifts, 213. Apostates, cast down by pride, 663. They are rulers of vices, 707. Christ is the Angel of Great Counsel, and how, 37, 44, 48. The faithful soul is denoted by a garden, 228; by the Blessed Virgin Mary, [Col. 1654] 9; and by a throne, 715, 716. Ruling over the senses, it is a queen, 520. Adorned with virtues, it is God’s seat, 601, and dwelling place, 620. In heaven it will see greater things than it hoped or believed, 422. There it always desires to be united with the body, 247. To be tested, it is temporarily deprived of divine consolation, 11. The sighs of the desolate soul toward God, 257. Deserted by God, it becomes foul, 585. How it is to be lost and found, 121. A fuller treatment of the Sunday of the Annunciation and Incarnation, 171. Antichrist is figured in Antiochus, 726. The understanding of one aspiring to conversion ought to be the Ancient of Days, 714. The apostles were foreseen by the prophets, 307. They see what the prophets desired, 317. By the coming of the Holy Spirit they become terrible to the Jews, 371. They make the Lord’s commandment luminous, 191, and by their preaching make Christ’s Passion salutary to us, 303. They conquer the Gentiles by the word, 304. They perform signs greater than Christ’s, 313. They obtain more from God than other saints, 315. They alone are princes over them, 317, and after the Blessed Virgin Mary are nearest to God, 301, 315. They are the days of the age, 694; Christ’s servants, 138; gatekeepers, 139; indeed, fathers, 756. They are also compared to a silver bowl, 163; their knowledge, to gold, 164; and to mountains, 367. Further praises of them, 305, etc. Their imitators are people of spiritual conduct, 321. Water signifies the knowledge of Scripture or the grace of compunction, 220; likewise original sin and concupiscence, 128; and actual sins, 252. The water of contradiction can denote the Jews, 320. How the eagle’s youth is renewed, and what it morally signifies, 394. The convert walks its way in heaven, 685. The bow was Christ stretched tight in the Passion, 753. The sand of the sea denotes the people before the Law, unfruitful, 694. The apostles are like silver; all desire them eagerly, 162, 703. The ram can indicate Christ or prelates who lead by example, 637, 638. Arms signify the defense of sin, 232. Aromatic spices are a symbol of virtues, 240. Christ’s Ascension into heaven is a pilgrimage, 138. Mystically, it is ours, 287. It is accomplished by charity, 288. It causes the devil the greatest sorrow, 353. How we ought spiritually to be roasted, 584. Avarice is denoted in the tollhouse, 580. Hearers of God’s word give drink to the preacher by putting into practice what they have heard, 624. What manner of divination is lawful, 352. The ear is a symbol of the appetite for human praise, 236. Gold is a symbol of knowledge of truth, 75. Gold, frankincense, and myrrh are developed mystically and morally, 72. God’s help is always ready for us, 261, especially for those wishing to repent, 412, and for those who implore it, 674. See “Grace.”

### B

Baptism is sanctified by Christ, 103. Through it we flow to Christ and become children of the Church, 451; branches of Christ, 292, 297; and are united with the other faithful, 484. Repentance is drawn from Sacred Scripture, 533. The Basilica of Saint Martin is consecrated by Christ himself, 603. Heavenly blessedness is Christ’s dominion, 36; a reward without end, 38; and is rendered back by the saints to Christ in thanksgiving for what they receive, 45. See “Heaven.” A fierce battle took place between Christ on the cross and the devil’s power, 324. Jacob’s blessings of his sons are applied to the orders of the Church and to the contemplative and active life, 729. The blessing of a preacher or prelate is the fruit of exhortations, 763. Saint Benedict: lamp of splendor, 429. Remembrance of divine benefits perfects us in fear and love, 444. How Bathsheba was a figure of the virginal Mother, 569. Everyone devoted to spiritual conduct considers the two ways, 570. Saint Blaise, a powerful patron, fears death of the soul more than death of the body, 125. God grants bodily goods to those asking, to be applied to his honor, 315. We must not only understand and love the good, but also put it into practice, 560. The arm denotes work and strength, 499.

### C
### C

Caesars of old demanded the kissing of their feet from subjects and suppliants, 145. The chalice signifies the Lord’s Passion, 455. The camel, an animal partly unclean, represents worldly affections, 90. The candlestick is a symbol of Christ’s Church, 424; of the holy bishops Martin and Udalric, 600. Captives, morally speaking, are those who do not return to their former sins, 29. Captivity was led captive by Christ in his Ascension, 346. Christ is the head of the good, the devil of the evil; a reward being reserved for each, 47. The intention is the head of thoughts, 222. The cardinal virtues, united together, overcome temptations, 405. Angels preside over them, 707; their opposite vices likewise, 707. The devil’s carnal suggestions are ineffectual in the hearts of the elect, 682, 710. A severe judgment awaits those who live carnally, 678. Chaste minds ought to be called God’s bedchamber, 732. A castle can be a symbol of the Blessed Virgin Mary, 470. Excessive chastisement is harmful, 233. See Mortification. The Blessed Virgin Mary is the chief exemplar of chastity and humility, 540, 611. She has obtained many imitators, 542. See Mary. Many preserve chastity through fear of disgrace, 220. It is compared to cinnamon and balsam, 508. Those exalted by their own honor or praise are to be called cedars, 107. Cedars drive away serpents by their scent, 506. Cedron signifies the hardness of the Jews, 228. The horned serpent, cerastes, signifies prudence and power in action, 745. Love of God and neighbor was pre-eminent in the Blessed Virgin Mary, 197, 536. It forbids unjust love, 631. It loves with all its strength, 537. It obtains from God the cleansing of sins, 293. From it come steadfastness and firm hope of eternal blessedness, 742. It is likened to fine flour mixed with oil, 644; likewise to oil, 447. It ought to stand out in prelates, 392.

Christ offers his kindness to the human race, 1 and 2. Moses as an infant and an adult, striking the Egyptian; the horn of oil; Joseph the growing son; and Elijah in the cave are figures of him, 19, 24, 751, 755, 661. He preserved the angels, 754. His crown is his humanity, 185, in which he did and suffered ineffable things for us, 475. His beauty shines in the Incarnation, his strength in the Passion, and his power in the Resurrection, 42. His infancy is compared to a shoot and a fountain, 542. He alone is without sin, 751. He journeys among Gentiles and Jews, 650, and graciously calls the Gentiles, 654. He is the teacher of humility, 104; exposed to the arrows and exasperations of sinners, 752; and he alone has power to lay down his life, 26. He was sorrowful for us, not because of death, 185. He becomes a whole burnt offering for our sins, 165; dies for his Church, 251; and in his Passion became a golden censer, 325. He is both sacrifice and example for us, 637. He is the broken bow, 753. He brings the fathers out of limbo, 754. His soul desires to be united with its body in the Resurrection, 249. In rising again he is strong as a lion, 237; the Sun of righteousness, 242. Ascending into heaven, he departs as a traveller, 138, leading captivity captive, 346. By his humanity, he is leaning upon his beloved, 556. He is still troubled in his members, 39, 402, and is purified in them, 111. Though needing glory from no one, he willed that we should share in his glory, 461. He will be Judge, 500. He will graciously meet the righteous in death, 102. He is compared to a fish and a honeycomb, 263; to the vine, 290, 298; to an angel, 323; to Noah’s ark, 248, 249; to a grain of wheat, 459; to rich earth, 660; and to Lebanon, 544. In preaching he is thunder, 366. The food of the soul is repentance and doctrine, 690.

Circumcision of the heart is better than circumcision of the flesh, 629. Watchfulness of mind closes off entry to the tempter, 231, 440, and fosters the sweetness of contemplation, 465. It is commended by Christ, 233.

[Col. 1656] There are two keys in the Church: knowledge and power, 152. Heaven is often gained by a small deed and good will, 72; yet only by leaving the world, 132; through hardships and labors, 259, 453, 458. Those coming to it must cross a river, 557. It awaits the baptized, penitents, holy martyrs, and confessors, 506, 557, especially the continent, 695. Its possession is without loss, 662, 692. It resounds with the praise and thanksgiving of the saints, 385, 388. Our sins have made it a far country, 205.

The mystical Supper of the Lord is prepared by fear and love, 56, and by compunction, 27. Human thoughts are like the sea, 89. Thoughts of sin without consent need not necessarily be disclosed in confession, 296. Evil thoughts introduce various temptations, 262. They are scourges by which the demon tears souls apart, 331, and annihilates virtues, 711. In this world they are rarely clean, 223. Their purity must be sought from God, 221. The Blessed Virgin Mary guarded their intentions with the greatest care, 493.

Knowledge of what ought to be done and omitted is supremely necessary, 136, especially knowledge of sins for the salvation of the soul, 83. Knowledge of God and of oneself constitutes the days of the mind: morning and evening, 416, 734. This knowledge and love are the single eye, 428. It calls forth tears of repentance, 633. God assists it, 269, and also establishes it in perfection, 413. It is figured by angels at the tomb, 279, and by gold, 75.

The dove harms no one, 331. It is a symbol of charity and simplicity, 490. In Naomi it figures Christ’s soul, 248. The pillar of cloud and fire shines more brightly for religious than for secular persons, 626. Compassion toward the failings of subjects and rejoicing with them, and so forth, are the two breasts of prelates, 605. Compunction restores us as a seat of the divine Majesty, 398. It prepares in the heart a banquet pleasing to the Lord, 583. It is sweet wine, 741, and the bread of the soul, 749; yet it has no savor for those who do not know how to govern themselves, 749. It is figured in Moses, 259, and is like a furnace of fire, etc., 132.

Concupiscence is not only lust but also toil of the soul, 157, and a dark night, 578. Confession is an act of great strength, 89; it makes us stronger, 527. It must be made by the tongue of heart and action, 722. It is necessary for the penitent, 634, and must not be delayed, 90. Examination should precede it, 614, 632. It gives glory to God, 83, and a kiss, 441. It opens the understanding for searching the Scriptures, 409. God requires confession of his divinity amid dangers and persecutions, 145. Christ’s confessors shine in teaching, life, and examples, 192. They are compared to an exalted palm, 506. Shame moves many to preserve chastity, 220. God removes this shame from sinners, 3.

The congregation of the righteous is Christ’s dwelling-place, 230, where we are in Christ and Christ in us, 296. It is full of consolation, 740. Before the veneration of the Holy Cross it endured many assaults of the demon, 321; against him it is now a stronghold, 643. It is a city of refuge, 641, and like a vineyard, 740. See Church. Married persons may be called kings, 669. Mercy brings them to salvation, 695. Job is their type, 696. Conscience is like a book, 718. When polluted, it does not understand divine mysteries, 702. Consent is either good or evil and is like a yoke, 158. Through reflection, vicious affections are weakened, 712.

The evangelical counsels were unheard of by the patriarchs, 37, 63. They raise mortals to supreme perfection and immortality, 44. The fifth counsel is drawn from the gifts of the Holy Spirit, and differs from a commandment, 628. Christ grants abundant consolation to those willing to do penance, 586, 676, and the greatest consolation to those devoted to good works, 238. See Sweetness and Heavenly Visitation. The Blessed Virgin Mary is an example of constancy, 200; likewise the holy apostles Philip and James, 311. Habit casts the sinner down into graver sins, 703.

Contemplation must issue in work and benefit for others, 58. It enlightens the mind, 124; teaches discernment, 736; perfects love, 241, 444; makes the soul young again, 687; confirms it in good, 750; fills the mind with sweetness, 70, 574; and unites the spirit to God, 416. It is a precious pearl, 130, a candlestick of light, 727. It is figured by a pair of turtledoves, 114, and hindered by concern for temporal things, 465. The continent are kings of Israel, 670. They live a heavenly life upon earth, with great merits, 695.

Contrition, like ointment, appeases the divine Judge, 241. It is signified by the powder of the perfumer, 512. The beginning of conversion is separation from secular business, etc., 438. It is a joyful Paschal day for the Lord, 215. The demon sends grievous temptations against one aspiring to it, 67. God aids one who is wavering, 268, and helps by heavenly inspirations, 581. Yet that person’s understanding ought to be ancient of days and mature, 715.

[Col. 1657] Gospel parables indicate what a convert ought to do, 127. There are three orders of converts: simple persons, soldiers, and canons and nuns, 90. They must change their intentions, words, and works, 674. Bodily and spiritual banquets are compared with one another, 582. Christ does not reject the Pharisee’s bodily banquet, in order to convert Magdalene, 435. For our conversion and redemption are Christ’s most pleasing spiritual banquet, 351, 582. Joseph’s banquet was a figure of the Supper of the Lord, 303.

The human heart is the fountain of thoughts, 262; an embittered sea, 707; and like a castle, 259. A contrite heart is signified by the alabaster vessel of ointment, 438. It ought to be united to God by love, 630. Humble and mourning, it receives the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, 377. Deserted by God, it becomes foul, 585; hardened, it shrinks from no crime, 704. The horn filled with oil signifies Christ the Redeemer, 24. God gives the blessed a crown instead of ashes, 31. One crown of Christ was his Incarnation and another his Passion, 183.

God grants bodily goods to those who ask, yet they must be applied to his honor, 315. Although the body is a symbol of corruption, 280, and hinders the vision of God, 294, Christ nevertheless longed after death to be united with his own body, 249. As it was a companion in merit during each person’s life, so it will be a companion in reward in heaven, 247. After the resurrection it is glorified, 335, 466. The gridiron signifies our body, 468. Accusation is a powerful temptation against the righteous, 411. The sign of the Cross drives demons away even from unbelievers, 322. It is the altar in Christ’s Church, 323. Its true worship consists in mortification, 328. It is borne by Christ, 37. The cross of Christ is one thing, that of sinners another, 120; how it should be borne, 121. Curiosity exposes the soul to the danger of sin, 171, 231.

### D

The condemnation of the reprobate is represented by a branch not remaining in the vine, 299. Daniel is the example and figure of the continent, 696. The beheading of St John signifies a heart emptied of God’s grace, 534. The joy of dedicating the mystical temple is brought about through grace and virtues, 728. Defense of sin makes it most grave, 232, and precipitates one into graver sins, 703. Pleasure without consent is free from guilt, 232. One devoted to it always becomes worse, 531, 532. One who does not resist it loves his soul so as to destroy it, and conversely, etc., 464. Christ’s delights are holy souls in the Church, 556. The desert may be called the world or the sinner’s heart, 511; likewise, the world after Christ’s departure, 557. Desire for eternal life may be called the virginal son of a converted soul, 196. It makes persons worthy of heaven, 226, and of God’s blessing, 339. It is nourished by the meaning and understanding of Holy Scripture, 196. In his desire for our redemption, Christ on the Cross was impatient of delay, 186. Desires, not sins alone, must be left behind, 182, 400. In this world they are never satisfied, 598. Despair is suggested by the infernal enemy to one who is about to do penance, 186.

What the harm of the soul is, and whence it comes, 122. God sees all things as present, including future things, 466. Where he is, all goods are; where he withdraws himself, there is nothing, 310. He is beheld by the elect in four ways, 341. No one should come before his sight empty-handed, 363. Remembrance of him drives away evil thoughts, 427. He shows himself a father to sinners, 216, especially in the New Testament, 333. He does not allow sinners to be put to shame, 3, offering mercy even to the unwilling, 194, as though he did not know their sins, 442. Yet the reprobate resist him, 211. He rewards our labors in heaven, 274. He is to be loved above all things, 391. In order to make the righteous more fervent in love, he often leaves them apparently alone, 283.

Devotion is compared to ointment, 241; it should be opposed to the appetite for vainglory, 241. The right hand of God, mystically, is full of length of days to be bestowed upon the saints, etc., 454; it signifies good works, 140. The devil always schemes how to overthrow us, 331. He never ceases from temptations, 206. At first he suggests small matters, 526, and at last despair, 586. He tempts in matters we consider holy, 233. After the redemption he rages more fiercely, 726, especially against those to whom God sends grace, 230, 234, and against souls about to depart from their bodies, 420. But he is conquered by the sign of the Holy Cross, 321. His strength must be kept before the mind’s eye, 330, as must his malice and cunning, 682. He believes and confesses Christ’s divinity, 230, and is greatly afflicted by Christ’s Ascension, 353.

[Col. 1658] How one ought to be God’s servant, 364. The tempter is figured in Herod, 65; in Iscariot, 230; in Alexander, 723; and in the insatiable lion, 683. The day signifies the coming of the Holy Spirit and the remission of sins, 250. One day is given that inspires, another that breathes out, and finally one that breathes toward heaven, 606. Difficulties which the senses set against the way of salvation are overcome by constancy and God’s mercy, 577.

Beautiful love is found in Christ alone, 516. Our love, in comparison with his divine love toward us, is nothing, 445. It is threefold: beginning, progressing, and perfecting, 374. Without it no one is saved, 376. It must be added to repentance, 282. It and hope snatch the sinner from the jaws of hell, 150. It is called the cup of the Lord, 456. In the apostles it is increased by the coming of the Holy Spirit, 379. In God toward us it makes no distinction or partiality, 449. Mary seeks her beloved, though she has him present; and this is because of her love for us, 198. Discipline is not knowledge alone, but also the ordering of conduct, 560. Christ’s divinity was hidden from the devil, lest our redemption be impeded, 482. To leave riches is a work of the greatest difficulty, 366. Whoever teaches another abounds in doctrine, 89. What sorrow is good and pleasing to God, 730. What leaving one’s house signifies allegorically and morally, 137, 139; it is to suppress evil will, 399. How we ought to become a spiritual house, 615. The Blessed Virgin Mary is the house of divine Wisdom, 609. The gifts of the Holy Spirit bring a person to eternal blessedness, 267. They dwell in Christ, 470. The Spirit’s inward sweetness is the Lord’s portion, 222, and Christ’s bread, 260. Whoever tastes it always thirsts for more, 260. It overcomes temptations, 263. The soul bears its loss with grief, 257. When invoked by us, God removes hardness of heart, 243. The hardness of the Jews is signified by the torrent Cedron, 228.

### E

Drunkenness and gluttony are the mother of lust, 709. Christ’s Church is gathered from Jews and Gentiles, 16. It is formed through pressures and sufferings, 424. It unites us to Christ, 296. It is Christ’s garden, 228; temple, 323; and candlestick, 424. It is partly in heaven and partly on earth, 324. It consists of a threefold order: prelates, penitents, and innocents, 166; to which a fourth, the obedient, is added, 596. It prays for all, 453. It is figured in the mother of the sons of Zebedee, 450; in the earth, 552; and it began before Christ’s time, 552. The elect are one body with Christ, 403. Elijah in the cave is a figure of the Son of God before and after the Incarnation, 661. Emmaus signifies imperfection and lukewarmness, 254. Christ will be ashamed of one who is ashamed of him, 123. The Eucharist should not be received without prior preparation, 23. It fortifies us against the demon, 364. In it Christ pretends, as it were, not to know our sins, 442. It is the mystery of our redemption, 475. It makes us Christ’s blood-relatives, 620. Wandering of the mind exposes one to danger of sin, 171, and gives entrance to temptation, 231. Those who observe evangelical and apostolic teaching will draw salvation from the Lord, 561. A thorough examination must precede confession, 614, 632. Those who do not imitate the example of the righteous may be called unbelieving and hard of heart, 342. A person reproaches himself when he repents, 340.

### F

In Holy Scripture, “made” signifies something great and singular, 581. Dregs signify the operation of sin, 232. Human favor and accusation are vehement temptations, even against the righteous, 411. See Vainglory. Windows signify our senses, 310. In the Old Testament, hay was the whole human race devoured by the ox, the devil, 14. The feasts of the apostles should be celebrated more solemnly than others, 303. A feast day is to pass from evil to good, 215. A faithful servant is not one who hunts after vainglory in good works, 434. The steadfast have great faith; the inconstant, little faith, 263. Christ is its foundation, 693. Without good works it does not exist, 340. It merits for Peter the keys of the kingdom of heaven, 148. It is signified by water, 446, and by the roots of the mystical mountain, 370. Daughters signify weakness, 752, 758.

[Col. 1659] We were children of the devil and of the world, 738. By considering the end, we overcome temptation, 439. Christ may be called the flower of the field, 15. The river to be crossed by those coming to heaven is that of baptism, repentance, or suffering, 557. The Lord is an inexhaustible fountain, 561. The fountains are the Savior’s baptism and repentance, 94. Fortitude, the fourth of the gifts of the Holy Spirit, is necessary against temptations, 628. See Cardinal Virtues. Christ and the angels are our brothers, 737. The fruits borne by one who remains in Christ are enumerated, 299. Christ is the fruit of honor and uprightness, 516. Flight in persecution may lawfully be undertaken after Christ’s example, 680. Lightnings are symbols of Christ’s miracles, 367. The smoke of spices is Christ’s Passion, drawing tears from the eyes, 327, 510.

### G

The archangel Gabriel is figured in the dew of heaven, 167. What he foretold the Blessed Virgin Mary about Christ, and how it was fulfilled, 175. The hen, zealously protecting her chicks, intimates Christ’s love for us, 53. Gideon rising by night is a figure of Christ’s birth, 33. The generation of the Son of God from the Father’s womb is explained, 41. Although in some manner hidden from God, the Gentile people aspire to salvation, 423, 653. In five persons it obtains great hope of salvation from Christ, 654. It is planted by Christ in his Church, 229. It finds salvation in the sacred things possessed among the Jews, 655, who vainly begrudge it to them, 651. One is still a Gentile, though Christian, who lives the life of the Gentiles, 517. Christ to be incarnate is called the Branch because of the hope of the very abundant fruit to follow, 542. The two-edged sword is fear and love of God, 236. Heavenly glory changes human minds, 225. Vainglory is sought by all through nature, 385, and suggested by the demon to all, 235, 411, 737, especially to the righteous, 718. It must be resisted, and how, 244. It destroys innocence before God, 597; deprives one of the merit of good works, 68, 140, 425, 587, 591, 718; and takes away inward consolation, 584. It is compared to the right ear, 236; to darkness, 578; and to the little horn of Daniel’s beast, 712. The grain of wheat is Christ, 459; fruitful in the martyrs, 461; and a symbol of every human being, 462. God’s grace enlightens us so that, leaving the world, we may go from virtue to virtue, 3, 4, 6. It changes a hard heart into a garden, 229; breaks vicious inclinations, 85; cleanses affections, 221; is present in temptations, 440, 761; sustains us in prosperity and adversity, 219; and works every supernatural thing in and with us, 76, 345, 385, 434, 437. It is wicked not to cooperate with it, 425. It visits us in various ways and at various times, 142. Knowledge depends upon God’s choice, not ours, 340. The demon strives to hinder its fruit, 67. It is empty in the unrepentant sinner, 357, 534. It is compared to a precious tunic, 272, and to a very dense cloud, 367. Drops of rain signify the fathers of the Law, 694.

### H

Heresies make the approved manifest, 147. The goat signifies the spirit of the sinful person, 631. A human being in hardships is figured in a grain, 462. The outer person always opposes the inner, 672. God shows mercy even to a person still sinful, 587, indeed before the angels, 553. The garden is a symbol of the Church, 228, and of the faithful soul, 228, 282. The divine Guest must be received with greater purity than a human guest, 17. Christ’s humanity is the bride leaning upon her beloved, 556. The shoulder signifies labor, 36, 43, 48. God reveals his mysteries to the humble, 156, and bestows upon them the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, 377. Humility is taught by Christ’s doctrine, 104, and by example, 144, 699. It judges itself unworthy of God’s benefits, 99; in considering them it troubles the elect, 408; and it esteems its own merits as nothing, 445. It preserved the holy angels, 589, and innocence, 597. It is the beginning of our redemption, 490. It made Mary the Mother of God, 515, and Matthias an apostle, 160. It disposes one for repentance, 279; merits grace, 339, the Holy Spirit, 358, 407, and obtains forgiveness of sins, 94. It is a remedy against temptations, 161, 406; raises the mind above passions, 419; gives peace of heart, 349, 355, 744; gives merit to works, 73; and preserves them, 738. It is the mother of virtues and opens heaven’s gate, 591. This virtue is especially necessary for prelates, 732.

[Col. 1660] It is signified by dust, 590; by a little child, 513; is like a hated woman, 690; and like nard, 470. Hypocrisy: see Vainglory.

### I

The fire of hell will burn sinners allegorically in this world, and truly in the next, 300. The fire of charity never says, “Enough,” 686. Ignorance, whence it arises, greatly disturbs a convert in a good resolve, 268. What it is like in the sinner, 631. Because of it sinners have cities of refuge, 640. One who acts with it does not act as a human being, 708. It is the mother of harmful security, 657. Not every divine illumination in a person is carried into action, 266. What Christ’s dominion upon the shoulder is, 36. The ungodly hate the preachers of the divine word, 49. The unrepentant person is stripped of heavenly goods, 213. Imprudence is like a winged lioness, whose wings are ignorance and forgetfulness, 708. The day of the Lord’s Incarnation was the most longed-for of all, 156, 181. Angels marvel at its mystery, 387, 289. Inconstancy is perpetual in this world, 60. It is like a leopard with four heads and wings, 710. Unbelief is failure to agree with faith in one’s works, 340. We ought always to remember our weakness, 330. St James the Apostle asks God to forgive his enemies, 311. Injustice is compared to Daniel’s fourth beast, 711, 719. God looks upon innocence safeguarded by humility, 597. Innocence is the youth of the soul, 518. Those resisting heavenly inspirations stone the prophets, 53. If we cooperate with these inspirations, they bring conversion to completion in us, 581, 717. Understanding, the sixth gift of the Holy Spirit, is acquired by purity of heart, 629. Joined to good works, it sustains the soul, 740. Intemperance is like a bear, 709. Intention placed before works produces merit or demerit, 425, 700. Concupiscence and pleasure especially lie in wait for good intention, 532. It ought to be pure in a preacher and prelate, 766. Its symbols are the eye, 427, and the head, 632. We are questioned by God so that we may know ourselves, 270. According to our merits, we shall see the invisible God with invisible senses, 286. Irrational sense is like a millstone, 592. The upper watering is grace; the lower, compunction, 436. Isaiah vainly sets before ungodly Ahaz the immensity of divine goodness, 193.

### J

Praise of the Apostle James, 305, 308. He is compared to a dove at the windows, 308. He is cast down from the pinnacle of the temple, 310. He is tempted by the Jews as Christ was by the devil, 319. Jesus signifies the human being to be saved, 232. See Christ. By equal endurance of hardships Job, the righteous man, merited the greatest glory, 453. He is a type of married persons, 696. Joseph’s banquet is a figure of the Supper of the Lord, 303. The Jews glory in the western letter of the Law, 645, and in their own and their fathers’ merits, 646. They begrudge salvation to the Gentiles, 651. The Blessed Virgin Mary laments that they are to be abandoned by mercy, 177. They will be converted at the end, 352. Without their king, each does what seems right to himself rather than to God, 650. Judas Iscariot is a type of the devil, 230. By doing penance we forestall the final judgment, 597, 676, and by judging ourselves, 718. Christ’s yoke is sweet: it is consent with him, 159. Justice is the same virtue as humility, 406. Divine justice and mercy are the Lord’s feet, 438. Both must continually be kept before the eyes, 559. Grace and innocence are the youth of spirit and soul, 518.

### L

By constant labor and humility one reaches glory, 259, 453, and God’s abundant reward, 275. Milk signifies the weak, yet those intent upon good works, 88. Tears of compunction and remembrance of inward sweetness are elicited by remembrance of the Lord’s Passion, 327. Wool signifies warmth and, mystically, divine love, 716. To languish for God’s love is to disdain all things except God, 204. A *laterna* (lantern) signifies sinful consent, 232. Divine mercy snatches the thief on the cross from the jaws of hell, 324.

[Col. 1661] St Lawrence enters heaven like a most powerful prince, 462. Let him be an example to us in the fires of temptations, 468. Praise of God alone ought to be intended in all works, 96, 385. It is rendered to God by the saints in heaven, 385, 388. To give this praise to God for conversion is the completion of perfection, 721. Self-praise is suggested by the devil and deprives one of merits, 68. It should therefore not be sought, 76. God will render it to each person on the last day, 96. The winged lioness signifies imprudence, ignorance, and forgetfulness, 708. How, pursuing the ravisher of her cubs, she is delayed and deceived, 707. Sacred reading is necessary for the soul, 762. The lion signifies the devil, 657, 673; likewise a prelate, and the cubs his subjects, 139. The leper is healed, when Christ consecrates St Martin’s church, by removal of his skin, 604. Leviathan figures the demon or Herod, 679. Levity in words and deeds is difficult to correct, 710; it often does not come from the heart, 710. The Law was made immaculate through Christ’s Ascension and the coming of the Holy Spirit, 190. It is signified by fire, 666. A book ought to be God’s access to our heart, 100. What binding and loosing signify morally, 154. Our work ought to be like a lily, 606. The lily signifies humility, chastity, and charity, 606. The tongue in confession must be twofold: that of heart and action, 722. Linen is a symbol of purity of heart, 219. Washing of feet signifies cleansing of affections, 221. A lamp is a type of Christ’s humanity, 423. Mourning is followed by consolation and strength, 30, and by joy, 31. How the moon burns by night, 141. Christ arms those obliged to undergo the fury of wolves, 329. Wolves signify infernal spirits, 329, 331. In one sense, whoever wishes to be saved ought to imitate wolves, 731.

### M

The Magi, or the holy Three Kings, are figured by Pharaoh’s daughter at the river, 20. They themselves are a type of converts, 66. God’s magnificence is his mercy, 106. “The Majesty of the Lord” is a name of fear, 698, 705. The brightest morning is the Lord’s Incarnation and Resurrection, 365. What it is to remain in God is explained, 290, 297. The meek receive the Holy Spirit, 358. Meekness is figured in the lamb, 392. It is the Lord’s way, 559. The sea signifies the heart of a person aspiring to repentance, 707. Precious pearls are virtues, especially contemplation, 130.

The Virgin Mary was preordained by God, 554; born from David’s line, 169. She is concerned for the salvation of humankind, 170, 174, 198, 536, for which she acts as an envoy before God, 482. She is mediator between God and human beings, 34. She was the first to vow virginity to God, 168, 540. She excels in the cardinal virtues, 469, 609; in the theological virtues, 197, 611, 490; especially in love of God and neighbor, 536, 547, 612; and in humility and chastity, being higher than the angels, 495, 540, 546, 555, 611. Many now imitate these virtues, 542. She contemplates divine mysteries, 483, is filled with heavenly joy, 187, and instills the sweetness of the divine word in others by both exhortation and example, 495. She removes the reproach of women, 562. The services she rendered to Christ are enumerated, 487. She is sorrowful in the persecution and Passion of her Son, 486; she has compassion on him in his suffering, 612; yet she prays for those who crucify him, 613. She is a most merciful mother, 34. She helps those invoking her, 170, 483, 499, 492, 543, and her intercession does not permit the sinner to perish, 511. She can never be praised enough, 562. She is the foundation of our faith, 573; the house of divine Wisdom, 469; the eastern gate, 480; a well and fountain, 542, 543; Jacob’s ladder, 546; and a column of smoke from spices of myrrh and incense, 510. She is compared to a castle, 479; to the sun, 184, 198, 199; and to the earth, 168, 541, 573. The women listed in the book of Christ’s genealogy were figures of her, and how this is so, 563. As betrothed to Joseph, she is a type of the faithful soul, 9.

Martha is a type of Christ’s humanity, 473, 474. St Martin is compared to an olive tree and a candlestick, 599. His basilica is consecrated by Christ himself, 603. Martyrs burn with love, 192. They are a grain of wheat, 461, and are compared to roses planted in Jericho, 506. Mother signifies earthly manner of life, 400. Humility raises Matthias to the apostleship, 160, 161. Christ is physician to those beginning to repent, 586. One accustomed to meditation can scarcely be torn away from God, 271. Meditation is kindled by desire for heavenly things, 337, and weakens the violence of evil thoughts, 426. See Contemplation. A mind recollected in God is most pleasing to him, 170.

[Col. 1662] The merits of the saints are unequal, 331. The greatness of their reward is measured according to them, 210. Christ performed miracles by his own power, 367, and willed that the apostles should accomplish greater ones than he, 313. The Lord’s mercy is like oil upon all works, 507. It enlightens the sinner, 285; calls from worldly cares to spiritual life, 3, 5; when implored, removes hardness of heart, 243; and wills, as it were, not to know our sins, 442. It is offered even to the unwilling, 193, 194. The ungodly commonly resist it, 211, and those wallowing in sins will scarcely attain it, 640. It especially regards the heart intent upon divine love, 151. God has bestowed the greatest mercy upon the Gentiles, 654, 660. Mercy is God’s magnificence, 106; his kingdom, 125; and one foot, while justice is the other, 438, 446, 473. Therefore neither alone should be kept before the eyes, 559. Three Masses at Christ’s Nativity are offered to God as Creator, Redeemer, and Rewarder, 35; likewise to Christ as God, Human Being, and Rewarder, 39. Christ is always present to the mission which he performs in us, 329. A monk or spiritual person ought mystically to offer God the three gifts of the Magi, 75. Monasteries are cities of refuge for sinners, 641. The mountain signifies the Blessed Virgin Mary or the Church, 665. A monument—*monens mentem*, “admonishing the mind”—warns us toward repentance, 277. Remembrance of death cleanses the soul, 79. The moment of death also anoints the righteous, 417, 418. There the demon also brings false accusations, 678, but Christ will aid, 102, 419, 678. Those who, by mortifying themselves, worshipped the Holy Cross will look upon this death, 328. Moral death is diverse, 396. The soul’s death is threefold: inward consent to sin, deed, and habit, 524. It is conquered by Christ’s death, 304, 477. What it is to taste death is explained, 124. To drink something deadly is to yield to evil suggestions, 344. Mortification is inspired by the Holy Spirit, 332. It breaks temptations of the flesh, 746; obtains remission of sins, 463, 686, 760; and is the first requirement for the spiritual banquet, 583. It is signified by myrrh, 510, 515. Whoever flees it easily falls, 673. It must be moderated with discernment, 100; otherwise it does not please God, 735. In it consists the true worship of the Holy Cross, 328. The three dead persons raised by Christ signify the threefold death of the soul, 524. Moses is a figure of Christ, 19, 21. Woman is a type of the soul softened by grace, 437; more often, however, a type of soft living, 280; of persons inexperienced in good works, 281, 383; and of weakness, 472. The women weeping at the tomb were deemed especially worthy of the appearance of the risen Christ, 239. The women not praiseworthy who are inserted in Christ’s genealogy are included for the consolation of sinners, 563. Mary the Mother of God removed their greatest reproach, 545. Perfect purity of thoughts and affections will first be attained in the life to come, 223. The world is like the sea and a swift river, 2, 8. Everything in it fluctuates through inconstancy, 60, and is fleeting, 451. Its gain is pleasure, vanity, and pride, 122. The gifts of the holy Three Kings are mystically explained, 72. Myrrh signifies mortification, 510, 512.

### N

Three days of Nativity are celebrated in the Church: those of Christ, the Blessed Virgin Mary, and St John, 545. A little boat signifies the Church and the spiritual congregation, 402; likewise the humbled soul, 417; and heavenly rest, 414, 422. A ship is a symbol of spiritual or monastic life, 7, 268, 270, 402, 687, navigating through prosperity and adversity, 687. Negligence is the origin of perdition, 87. Human wickedness is like Nebuchadnezzar’s statue, 702. Noah is a type of prelates, 696. The name of the Lord Jesus—Wonderful, Counsellor, etc.—is explained, 62. How the most sweet name of Father in God is to be honored, 334. A name generally conveys knowledge of a thing, 400. Novices constant in fervor are called daughters running over the wall, 758. The night of the Lord’s Nativity is full of grace, 33. The flying cloud is a type of St Philip the Apostle, 308; likewise of every elect person, 309; and of the Holy Spirit and his gifts, 720. The number three signifies the Holy Trinity, 275; seven, the Holy Spirit, 250, and his gifts, 635; ten, the human senses and the commandments of the Decalogue, 620; eleven, transgression, 338; twelve, perfection, 359; fifty, repentance, 275, works of justice, 444, and perfection, 443; seventy, the ten commandments of the Decalogue and the gifts of the Holy Spirit, 635; likewise seventy, 164; one hundred, 163, 275, 635; and two hundred, 273. These signify perfection.

### O
Mercy of the Lord freely offers itself to the obedient, 220. Obedience is learned from Christ’s example, 474. It is the foundation of the spiritual building, 610, 614. It merits God’s grace, 390. Forgetfulness and ignorance are the nurses of imprudence, 708. The eye indicates the intention of an action, 427. A wicked eye indicates ignorance, 428. The fragrance of ointment is a symbol of repentance, 441. The oil of gladness is the charity of the saints in heaven, 31. Shining, refreshing, and healing, it is a symbol of Saints Martin and Ulrich, bishops, 599. Likewise, of love for God and neighbour, 636. Good works must be practised by one aspiring to perfection, 136. Not from an intention of vainglory, 68, 140. They shut the senses against the devil, 602. And they will receive abundant recompense from God, 239. To these must be added the guarding of the tongue and thoughts, 240. Many things that seem good to us are evil before God the judge, 420. Prayer must be made with the mind recollected, 170. And attentive, 455. Reconciled with one’s brother, 452. And above all for spiritual goods, 301. And heavenly goods, 452. And not by one praying for himself alone, 453. Without ceasing, which is accomplished by a good intention, 136, 437. It must precede contemplation, 750. It frees from temptations, 748. Its sweetness makes a person near to heaven, 131. And, from a chaste mind, it is offered to God by angels, 201. It is like incense, 165. Like a fiery and swift stream, 716. The Blessed Virgin Mary is an example of perseverance in prayer, 200. The prayer which the saints render in heaven is praise, 404. The Lord’s Prayer is mystically expounded concerning the saints in heaven, 334. There are three orders in the Church: prelates, penitents, and innocents, 166. And a fourth, of the obedient, 596. Likewise, those who are married, continent, and prelates, 669, 694. Their figures, 694. Original sin cast humankind into destruction and death, 323, 326. It is a heavy burden, 551. Its lamentable effects, 725. The kissing of feet was formerly paid to Caesars, now to Roman pontiffs, 145. The Most Holy Trinity honours the Blessed Virgin Mary with a kiss, 197.

## P

The mantle of glory is the body reunited with the soul in the resurrection, 32. Palms in the hands of prelates are good subjects, 598. Every baptized person is a branch in Christ, 292. We ought morally to wear priestly vestments within ourselves, 457. Easter, that is, “passing over,” is the conversion of a person pleasing to God, 215. It is the greatest of feasts and full of consolation, 239. It is prefigured in the solemnity of unleavened bread, 363. Although the Passion disturbed Christ’s humanity, 477. So that he might draw the bow, 753. And pierce it as a censer, 325. Yet it was for him a day of joy, 185. And of glory, and for us of grace, 326. Breaking open the barriers of hell and opening the gate of paradise, 15, 16. Making us sons from servants, 559. It is an example to be fulfilled invisibly in us, 227. Its imitators have nothing to fear, 244. It would not have benefited us unless the apostles had preached it, 303. Anyone can be a pastor to himself through reading, etc., 762. God began to be called Father only after Christ’s birth, 333. It is the sweetest name in God, 334. Patience of heart is gained through consideration of eternal things, 743. It is figured in the lamb, 392. Patriarchs are compared to mountains, prophets to hills, 552. Christ’s peace is threefold: from the devil, from vices, and from death, 261. And it is explained, 378. True peace is given in heaven, 378. Sinners are burdensome to God and to human beings, 193. They often do not wish their sins to be taken away from them, 212. They are adulterers before God, 523. Even in this world they already burn in a certain manner, 300. They are figured in Herod, 530. The intercession of the Blessed Virgin Mary rescues them from destruction, 511. The conversion of Saint Matthew gives hope to all, 579. Those doing penance are exalted in heaven, 422. Sin is committed through consent, 232. It becomes grave through action, and most grave through defence of it, 232. Open sin is not immediately suggested by the demon, 526. Many avoid this, but not inward sin, 153. It makes us servants, 689. And a meal for the devil, 530. It is a great disturbance, 666. It is figured by a she-goat, 631. In this God permits a person to fall, so that he may rise stronger, [Col. 1664] 217. No pure creature could erase it by making satisfaction, 25. It must be carefully examined by the penitent with discernment, 632. The Lord’s feet signify his Incarnation, but his hands his power, 262. They are mercy and justice, 438, 446, 473. Likewise, preachers, 679. Pilgrimage is a very arduous transition from secular to spiritual life, 430. No less so is that of Christ, the Son of God, among Gentiles and Jews, 650. There are still many perfect persons in the Church, 368. Prayer, knowledge, and action are necessary for one aspiring to perfection, 135. It is not enough to leave everything unless imitation of Christ is added, 397. Its completion is thanksgiving after conversion, 721. Perseverance in good, in addition to works, is necessary, 144. It leads to the joys of heaven, 418. The Blessed Virgin Mary is its example in prayer, 200. Saint Peter holds the keys of heaven through faith, 148, 139. Great glory shines in heaven, 143. Named by the angel at Christ’s resurrection, he gives hope to sinners, 245. Why he, James, and John were loved by Christ more than the others, 449. Praise of Saints Philip and James, 305. They are like a flying cloud, 308, 310. Piety, the second of the gifts of the Holy Spirit, is indicated through the Book of Exodus, 626. To fish mystically signifies to leave the world, 267. Fish signify Christ, 679. Our good senses, 271, 267. Most often, the devil, 679. One kind of weeping is outward, another in the heart, etc., 278. Rain is a symbol of the humility and chastity of the Blessed Virgin Mary, 540. The penitent ought to be like a bucket tied to a rope and lowered into a fountain, 94. He has God’s present help, 412. He is filled with the gifts of the Holy Spirit, 720. His tongue speaks anew, 355, 358. He turns evils committed into good, 575. The more gravely he sinned, the more ardently he becomes fervent in the love of God, 681. He is joy to the angels of God, 441. He does not fear the demon at death, 688. Mary Magdalene is his example, 437, 440. Penance is drawn from the reading of Scripture and hearing the word of God, 533. It beneficially troubles a person, 676. It kills vices, 719. It snatches a person from the jaws of hell, 681. It changes fear into love, 409. It makes kings, 689. It associates one with the saints, 596. It restores a person to the heavenly homeland, 644. It must be done with discernment, 735. By distinguishing sin from sin, 632. Just desires must attain it, 282. And humility, 339. And works, 635. It is a banquet received by the soul, 527. It is likened to an inundating flood [reading uncertain: *inhabitanti*], 109. To a furnace of fire, 132. To a sign unto the depths of hell, 195. To fragrance, 441, 741. To the sea, 272, 592. To snow, 715. And to earth not sated with waters, 685. The demon strives to hinder it, 586. Without conversion it is nothing, 734. The power of Roman pontiffs comes from Christ and the emperor Constantine, 146. What Roman pontiffs and Pharisees, likewise the cohort, may signify mystically is indicated, 231. We must all plunder spiritually, 732, 739. Let no one rashly investigate divine predestination; rather, let him commend himself to it through humble action and prayer, 61. What the preaching sent to the meek, the broken-hearted, captives, and the lame is, is explained, 28 ff. It is an offering acceptable to God, 634. It is like water, 731. Its blessing is fruit among its hearers, 763. Prayer must precede it, 766. And intention, 766. It is like Christ’s thunder, 366. Preachers ought to thirst for the salvation of their hearers, 623. And for the glory of God alone, 292. Not for human favour, 765. They should speak with discernment according to their hearers’ capacity, 622, 670. With humility and freedom, 360, 525. With confidence and a good conscience, 359. Let them move others by their example, 359, 393. Let them feed by word, work, and prayer, 393. Let them be insatiable, 684. Without the operation of the Holy Spirit they accomplish nothing, 376. They are called heavens, 101. Fathers of Christ, 756. And Mother, 538. The summit of prelacy is not free from danger, yet, when God wills it, it must be accepted, 393. For its power is not from human beings but from God, 504. He who knows how to be well subject ought to be raised to it, 671. It is full of labour and distraction, 395. A prelate should seek an increase of perfection in his subjects, 764. Wisdom is necessary to him, 629. He must excel in charity, 392. Suffer with and rejoice with his own people, 605. He may deservedly be called a prince, 630. He is figured in Reuben’s blessing, 730. In the lion, and his subjects in its cubs, 739. A greater reward in heaven awaits those who endure harder things, 120. It is rendered according to the measure of merits, 210. The Lord’s manger is figured in Moses’ basket, 19. And it itself is a type of monastic life, 75. The deep may be called penance, 592. The prophets sigh for Christ’s coming, 13, 14. They are Christ’s arms, [Col. 1665] 754. A person should be a prophet to himself, 677. Prosperity draws us into sin more easily than adversity, 530. Christ is our neighbour, 642. The greatest prudence is to seek the kingdom of God, 330. It acts with provident deliberation, 745. It is signified by the serpent, 745. A girl is a symbol of frailty, 531. He is called a child by the Lord who is foolish and weak in spiritual life, 269.

## R

How Rahab was a figure of the most chaste Mother, 566. A branch of green olive signifies Christ’s most holy flesh, 552. God draws near to one reflecting on his imperfection, 255. Reconciliation with one’s brother is necessary for one approaching prayer, 452. Redemption benefited us more than creation, 149. Its sacraments are the Passion, Resurrection, and Ascension, 350. For it we are exceedingly indebted to the Blessed Virgin Mary, 539. Spiritual refreshment consists in sacred reading, prayer, and tranquillity of mind, 158. Those who sin through ignorance have cities of refuge, 640. And these are monasteries, 641. Married persons are kings, 669. The continent more so, 670. As are those ruling their senses and affections, 725, 749. Kings signify the outward senses, and governors the inward senses, 332. The soul is a queen if it rules the senses, 520. Christ’s kingdom consists of the righteous, 334. This Christ hands over to the Father after the Last Judgment, 207. The kingdom of sin in us is concupiscence, 207. What we ought to leave, and how, is explained, 400. Forgiveness of sins is obtained from God in many ways, 448. Christ’s Resurrection and Ascension confirm in us hope of heavenly things, 503. And our own resurrection encourages the righteous more, etc., 245. To mend the net is to do penance, 8. Each person ought to be king and priest of himself, directing his actions to God, 194, 522. Indiscreet rigor displeases God, 735. The rose planted in Jericho signifies martyrs, 506. A penitent ought to be like a wheel, turning himself toward works, 716. Ruth is a figure of the Blessed Virgin, and how, 568.

## S

The true Sabbath is abstention from unlawful works, etc., 242. Each person ought morally to be a priest, 94, 522. And to wear vestments morally, 457. Sacraments are compared to roots, 503. Christ’s sacrifice benefits all, 26. The sacrifices of the Old Law were its figure, 324. Sacrifices of various kinds are described in the Book of Leviticus, 627. Lovers of the world are haters of humility, 95. And they neglect to avoid sins, 639. To leave the world is a great work, 268, 271, 314. Solomon is a figure of Christ, 183. Many angels attend the archangel as he greets Mary, 201. The angelic salutation is likened to the whisper of a gentle breeze, 667. The saints in heaven mutually perceive one another’s consciences, 386. They think of and desire the resumption of their bodies in the resurrection, 80, 335, 466, 386, 558. They suffer with our miseries, 336. And rejoice in the torments of the damned, 115. They existed before and under the Law, etc., 594. Sanctification in this life is not such as to exclude the capacity for sin, 23. What the shedding of blood mystically signifies, 52. Christ’s blood, of infinite worth, is avenged upon the Jews, 313. Wisdom, the seventh gift of the Holy Spirit, is especially necessary to a prelate, 629. Why the Book of Wisdom is so called, 691. Satisfaction for sins must be made not from sadness and compulsion, 48. It perfects penance, 686. It breaks sinful inclinations, 719. Those who will render it to God ought to be like asses, 743. Scandal must be removed through edification, 284. Otherwise it is punished with eternal torments, 592. Knowledge is very necessary in churchmen, 153. True knowledge is that which knows what ought to be loved, etc., 373. It is compared to a lamp, 424. It is the third gift of the Holy Spirit, 627. The most learned scribe is one who puts into practice what he reads, etc., 133. [Col. 1666] Meditation on Holy Scripture nourishes the sweetness of the Spirit, 130, 742. It is the Lord’s table, 520. And refreshment for the soul, 701. How it should be read, 618. Its sense is literal, spiritual, and intellectual, 529. Excessive security is the mother of negligence, and negligence of destruction, 87. It arises from ignorance, 657. The seat of divine majesty is the human being to be saved, 398. The twelve seats signify the inward and outward senses, 399. Holy Scripture may be called a harvest, 618. Old age is the languor and weariness of the soul, 518. Guarding the senses opens the intellect to understand spiritual things, 29. It must especially be observed by one converted, 273. The soul ruling them is a queen, 520. The inward and outward senses often do not agree, 710. Disturbing the mind, 576. God’s grace keeps both undefiled, 208. By the inward senses we merit the vision of God, 286. They are like cities, 209. Like servants, 431. Like goats, 638. The seven gifts of the Holy Spirit are signified by the first seven books of Holy Scripture, 625. Likewise by the seven days, 250. These seven days also signify the time from Christ’s Ascension to the end of the age, 253. The seventh day indicates the rest of soul and body, 513. What the six wings of the seraphim signify mystically, 699. Like serpents, let us strive first of all to preserve the head, 330. Serpents are a type of evil works, 343. Service rendered to God compels him to remain with us, 260. A sign unto the depths and a sign unto the heights are humble penance and the practice of virtues, 195. Fine flour mixed with oil expresses love for God and neighbour, 164, 636. He is not simple but double-minded who seeks human favour through good works, 392. How Christ’s left hand is full of riches and glory, 455. Those are said to dream who hear Christ’s divine Wisdom but do not follow it, 701. A cave can shadow forth Christ’s divinity, 661, 667. Christ, dying for sinners, gives them great hope, 326. And so does Matthew’s conversion, 579. Hope is signified by Magdalene’s kiss, 446. Thorns must be blunted by thorns, and how, 184. Spiritual persons ought to celebrate the feast of Pentecost more than secular persons, 353. The former are terrifying to the latter, 371. What spiritual vision is, 529. Spiritual life does not consist in a habit, 353. It is like a ship, 7. And its place is like a field, 128. By his coming the Holy Spirit anoints some and strengthens others, 27. He confirms the apostles, 17, 304, 472. He fills with gifts, 64. Through their preaching he works more than Christ himself, 368, 371. He is Paraclete, but not always, 377. He is the teacher of the divine word, 377, 379, 380. The prince of the world, 380. And the splendour of the saints, 41. He descends upon those to be baptized and forgives their sins, 105. He leaves no one empty of his grace, 206. He strengthens us against temptations, 332. How he is stable and mobile in us, 361. Working virtues in us, 519. The human spirit becomes God’s throne through contemplation, 698. Brides of Christ are to be consecrated only on the feasts of the Lord and the apostles, 318. How the stability and mobility of the Holy Spirit in us are to be understood, 361. The greatest folly is to serve sin, 690. A subject in the spiritual life ought to imitate lion cubs, 739. The cloth called a sudarium may be called the world, 211. The temptation of suggestions can occur without sin, 231. Yet it must be resisted at its beginning, 746. The devil’s temptations are very terrible, 711. The proud are imitators of the devil, 144. Pride makes us the house of Satan, 182. It is innate in evil spirits, 206. By it the demon tempts converts, 590. And the righteous, so that they may seek honour in good works and perseverance, 235. The synagogue envies salvation to the Gentiles, 652.

## T

Weariness is the destructive old age of the soul, 518. Various mystical exposition of the silver talent, 675. Likewise of five, two, and one talents, 431, 433. The universal Church of Christ may be called the temple, 323. We ourselves are God’s temple, 325, 699. Humility, Christ’s life, and Passion fill the temple of the heart, 698. What it is mystically, and its vessels and adornment, is explained, 727. Dedication produces joy, 728. Those who violate it are severely punished, 325. The time of divine visitation is uncertain to us, 137, 141. [Col. 1667] What little is expended by us in pious works is much before God, 433. Temptations are usually lighter at the beginning, 526. And lighter temptations are sent in by the demon, 331, 519. They press those aspiring to conversion, 67. They are more severe after conversion, 218. Even for the most perfect, 336, 747, 759. Yet they are not stronger than our strength and nature, 346. Many resist lighter temptations, but not heavier ones, 519. Earthly persons readily yield to them, 234. They are of three kinds: spiritual, bodily, and intellectual, 529. Human favour and accusation are very powerful temptations, 411. They are like fire, 468. They must be resisted with circumspection, 232, 405, 440. Sacred reading and prayer must be set against them, 86, 439. And the cardinal virtues, 405. Angels assist those who resist, 207. And God himself, 401. By whose grace they are overcome, 332. Victory over them is glorious for us, 87. And removes fear at the hour of death, 760. Christ teaches and instructs us to resist our tempters, Satan, the world, and the flesh, 159, 405. Satan the tempter is figured in Herod, 65. God spews out the lukewarm, 293. Most people meditate on earthly rather than divine things, 426. Earthly persons are easily cast down by temptations, 234. How Tamar was a figure of the Blessed Virgin Mary, 563. The theological virtues shine most excellently in the Blessed Virgin Mary, 490. They are the door of the kingdom of heaven, 561. They rescue from confusion and destruction, 570. They are the wings of the seraphim, 700. They are figured by water, a kiss, and oil, 446. Each person ought to offer a treasure to God, 71. The censer is a symbol of Christ suffering, 325. Frankincense signifies contemplation, 510, 512. Fear without love throws one into despair, 183. From this it arises, 12, 443, 698. It withdraws from evils, 46. It raises one dead in sins, 704. And regenerates spiritually, 625. It is the first of the gifts of the Holy Spirit, 625. One kind is servile or initial, another filial, 286. Reverential fear is found in the saints in heaven, 388. It is indicated by the name “child,” 36, 43, 46. Tobias is a figure of Christ, 679. Endurance of adversities arises from consideration of eternal things, 744. Christ’s preaching was like thunder, 366. A torrent is a symbol of a hardened heart, 229. Tribulation always assaults us in this life, 616. It fits us for the spiritual building, 615. The whole Most Holy Trinity pours grace into us, 86, 375, 431. It works together, 549, 666. It also accomplishes our redemption, 501. Its most holy mystery is drawn from the Book of Wisdom, 692. Christ’s sorrow unto death was not because of death, 185. A crowd signifies the disturbed senses and mind, 415.

## U

The breasts of a prelate are doctrine and example, likewise compassion and rejoicing with others, 605. And, for every person, contemplation and action, 605. Saint Ulrich is like an olive tree and a candlestick, 599. He prefers poverty to nobility, 603. Vengeance taken upon oneself pleases the Lord, 30. Anointing, which is the illumination of the Holy Spirit, is necessary for the preacher, 28. Ointment signifies contrition, devotion, and love, 240. A wife is a symbol of concupiscence, 400.

## V

The final words of those bidding farewell proceed from a sincere heart, 289. The veil of the temple signifies the good of modesty, 727. We obtain pardon from the Lord at small expense, 438. Christ’s final words are of the greatest importance and mystery, 289. To hear with the ear of the heart is a special grace, 376. The active and contemplative life are figured in Peter and John, 55. In Jacob and Israel, 574, 736. In Jacob’s sons, 733. By sons and daughters, 88. By doves and turtle-doves, 113. By the two evangelical servants making a profit, 208. They require prudence; they free us from inward temptations, 262. And lead to heaven, 504. The Most Holy Trinity works in us the transition from secular life and from sin to spiritual life, 432, 705. The present life never permits us to be perfectly united to God, 57, 722. It is never without gall and bitterness, 77. It is like a grain, 462. Vices are compared to beasts, 707, 719. The fruitful vine is the humility of the Blessed Virgin, 515. The fruit of the vine is charity, 292. It is a symbol of humility and obedience, 290. The alien vine is Adam, 290. The calf is a type of Christ’s human nature, 26. The manifold efficacy of the divine voice, 107. A good will makes works perfect, 273. Sustained by grace, it works salvation, 717. Conformed to the divine will, it leads us to knowledge of ourselves, 356. It is compared to a lamp, 424. To the wings of a seraph, 701. It easily changes for the worse unless preserved by divine grace, 68. An evil will must be abandoned along with its desires, 400. It is hidden in the heart as gold in a chest, 703. Pleasure carries a person away into sin, 533. It is the idol Baal, 672. And the daughter of Herodias, 530. Christ’s wounds are likened to the lights of heaven, 484. The spiritual things within us are fear and love, 202.

## DIPLOMATIC CODEX
I.—Charter of St Arnulf, bishop of Soissons, concerning the donation of the tithes of the town of Aldenburg to Aldenburg Abbey. 1565  
II.—Charter of Radbod, bishop of Tournai, concerning the liberty of the Church of St Peter the Apostle. 1567  
III.—Charter of Charles, count of Flanders, concerning the donation of tithes and of all the grain-revenue of the entire parish of Aldenburg. 1568  
IV.—Charter of Theodoric, count of Flanders, confirming the donations of Cono and Walter. 1569  
V.—Charter of Simon, bishop of Tournai, concerning the donation of the church of the Blessed Virgin Mary at Aldenborg, together with the integrity of the entire parish of Aldenburg. [Col. 1683] 1570  
VI.—Theodoric, count of Flanders, remits the annual rent from certain properties set out in the charter. 1571  
VII.—Charter of Walter of Heines, confirming the donations made by his father Cono and his paternal uncle Walter. 1572  
VIII.—Charter of Gerald, bishop of Tournai, by which the pledge of eight pounds against Walter of Vlaerdesloo is confirmed. 1573  
IX.—Charter of Pope Adrian concerning the confirmation of all the possessions of St Peter at Aldenborg—namely lands, tithes, offerings, and the parsonage. 1574  
X.—Charter of Bishop Gerald concerning the pledge of eight pounds from the altar of St Mary against Walter of Heines, confirmed by Count Philip. 1575  
XI.—Charter of Gerald, bishop of Tournai, concerning the parsonage of the church of St Mary of Aldenborg. 1576  
XII.—Philip of Alsace, count of Flanders, grants favour to Aldenburg Abbey, of the Order of St Benedict, in the diocese of Bruges. 1576  
XIII.—Charter of Philip, count of Flanders and Vermandois, by which are confirmed the donations of tithes from Oudenburg and from the parishes of Erneghem, Ichteghem, Conckelaere, and Bovekerke. 1577  
XIV.—Arnold, viscount of Ghistel, endows Aldenburg Abbey, with the approval of Philip of Alsace, count of Flanders. 1578  
XV.—Charter of Count Philip of Flanders concerning the confirmation of the tithes of the entire parish of Aldenburg. 1579  
XVI.—Charter of Everard, bishop of Tournai, concerning the agreement relating to the chapel of Zantvoorde and the abbot’s acquittal from the claim of the parishioners. 1580  
XVII.—Charter concerning all the great and small tithes of the parish of Aldenburg, adjudged to our church by Everard, bishop of Tournai. [Col. 1684] 1581  
XVIII.—Charter of Bishop Everard concerning the celebration of Mass in the chapel of Zautvoorde. 1581  
XIX.—Pope Celestine receives Aldenburg Abbey under his protection and grants it various privileges. 1583  
XX.—Charter of Baldwin, count of Flanders and Hainaut, by which are confirmed the donations of all tithes and of the church of Blessed Mary at Aldenborg. 1584  
XXI.—Charter of Guy, count of Flanders, concerning all the small tithes of the entire parish of Aldenburg and of Zantworde. 1585  
XXII.—The conferment of the scholastership of the town of Aldenburg, which belongs by full right to the abbot of Aldenburg. 1586  
XXIII.—Charter concerning the union of both portions of the pastoral care of the church of Aldenburg, effected by Remigius Driutius, bishop of Bruges. 1587  
XXIV.—Letter of Philip IV, king of Spain, to the marquis of Caracessa, in which he records that the proposed union of Oudenbourg Abbey with that of the Dunes had been under discussion. 1588  
XXV.—Protest made by the abbot and the religious of the Abbey of St Peter at Oudenbourg at the time of their departure from their house. 1588
